 Support workers, vote socialist, says Sanif
 By 
 Contributed 
 Nov 16, 2026
 Asyiqin Sanif is the Victorian Socialists’ Murray Plains candidate in the 2026 state election.
 Photo by
 Supplied
 With early voting in the Victorian election opening this week, The Riv has given all of the Murray Plains candidates one last opportunity to pitch themselves to voters.
 All candidates were offered 300 words to make their final appeal for votes.
 This article was written by Asyiqin Sanif, the Victorian Socialists’ candidate.
 It’s getting harder to live in the regional north.
 Hold tight - we’re checking permissions before loading more content
 Finding an affordable rental is unimaginable.
 Our severely constrained public transport means getting anywhere without a car is impossible.
 Childcare is unaffordable.
 Our teachers are overworked and underpaid.
 Waiting times for medical check-ups or for emergency medical services can take hours.
 Droughts caused by climate change heavily impact farmland and crops.
 Hot summers in towns with no beaches mean dealing with brutal heat and fear of bushfires.
 It doesn’t have to be like this.
 I’ll fight to make groceries cheaper, childcare free, decrease rent and build more public housing.
 I’ll expand public transport, public hospitals, Fire Rescue Victoria and make learning conditions better in our schools.
 Every home should be properly insulated, with air conditioning and solar panels installed cost-free.
 I’ll fight to build the first Medicare Urgent Care Clinics in Swan Hill, Cohuna and Echuca.
 The barrier isn’t economic — it’s political will.
 Growing up, I was elected as Echuca College vice captain and sat on the Campaspe Shire Youth Action Group committee.
 Since then, I’ve supported workers on strike at early morning pickets, organised protests to defend public housing, for climate justice, for LGBTQIA+ rights, for Palestine and against the rise of far-right Pauline Hanson.
 Every major party rules on behalf of the rich; Victorian Socialists are the opposite.
 That's why I pledge to only accept an average worker’s wage as my income if elected and will donate more than half of my salary to the community.
 Let’s show Victoria that Murray Plains rejects racism as the solution to the cost-of-living crisis.
 We think the solution is economic justice: take the wealth from the parasitic class and pour it into working-class communities.
 We deserve to live full and dignified lives too.
